title: Count Unreachable Pairs of Nodes in an Undirected Graph
summary: Given an integer n, you have an undirected graph with n nodes numbered 0 to n-1.
statement: Given an integer n, you have an undirected graph with n nodes numbered 0 to n-1. You are provided with a 2D integer array representing edges. Return the count of distinct node pairs that cannot reach each other.
constraints: Nodes are numbered zero through n-1 and edges are undirected.
A pair is unreachable when its two nodes belong to different connected components.
hints: Find every connected-component size with DFS or BFS.
After finding a component, pair its nodes only with nodes in components not processed yet.
Subtract size from remaining, then add size*remaining.
Each cross-component unordered pair is counted exactly when its earlier component is completed.
editorial: Each cross-component unordered pair is counted exactly when its earlier component is completed.

tests.explanation: Every node is connected, so there are no unreachable pairs.
The component sizes are four, two, and one, producing fourteen unreachable pairs.
